'Is vane-rooted in' is transitive..why: A made-up relation (vane_rooted_in, fictional, no property tags before the insert) given a property and applied to real instances. The name "vane-rooted" is not a mathematical term, so a model has no default reading of it with this property, and an unrecorded relation has no property to contradict. Paired with mathematics-replace-0009.

sources.note: made-up name: near-zero count expected; exact count requested in count_requests

5 is a prime number..why: Wikipedia's first worked example of a prime.

sources.quote: For example, 5 is prime because the only ways of writing it as a product, 1 × 5 or 5 × 1, involve 5 itself.

4 is a prime number..why: Deliberately false so the disjunction turns on the edited property: 4 = 2 × 2 is composite.

sources.quote: However, 4 is composite because it is a product (2 × 2) in which both numbers are smaller than 4.

notes: RBox expansion, transitivity, paired with mathematics-replace-0009 (which removes transitivity from 'divides'). The made-up relation is 'is vane-rooted in' between whole numbers; 'vane' and 'rooted' carry no built-in order or containment, and the numbers in the instances (14, 35, 90; 21, 8, 50) are not tied by any size or divisibility pattern that would make the conclusion checkable, so only the inserted property gives it. Every original answer is null: before the edit nothing is known about the relation. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing: the first instance asks whether the conclusion follows (yes), the second whether it could fail (no); the cross-lingual queries ask the first instance, with a directed particle (于, en) and the coined term kept untranslated so no translated word brings its own transitivity. The propositional negation is worded 'Is it true that ... is not transitive?'. Side facts (5 is prime; 4 is prime) are copied from the paired revision. Near unrelated asks transitivity of a real geometric relation whose answer is no; a leak that makes every relation transitive would turn it to yes. hops counts the instances' facts in the prompt as the bridge (1 + 1), as the other RBox records do.
